items.scene: Lena is offered tea or coffee. She says, 'I always pick tea when both are here.'
items.question: What does Lena prefer?
items.why_this_case_matters: Direct self-preference shown by a repeated voluntary choice.

items.scene: Noah does not speak, but every time he can choose, he goes to the park instead of staying home.
items.question: What does Noah most likely want to do?
options: He wants whatever his friend wants
items.why_this_case_matters: Preference is inferred from consistent voluntary choice, not from a stated plan.

items.scene: Mia says, 'I think Ben would rather have apples than oranges.'
items.question: What is Mia expressing here?
items.why_this_case_matters: Tests the common mistake of treating another person's preference as self-preference.

items.scene: Ravi is choosing a route for the team. He says the longer route is better because it is safer for everyone, even though he personally likes the shortcut.
items.question: Which route will Ravi choose?
items.why_this_case_matters: This is about goal and safety priority, not Ravi's own preference.
